sentence: This project builds an imaging method that detects the cardiotoxicity linked to cancer therapy early.
This project studies how a tumor suppressor gene works in T cells to fight tumors, using mouse genetics and clinical samples.
This project offers services that measure many metabolites in cells and tissue, using stable isotope tracers to study the metabolism of diseases such as cancer.
This project studies patterns of evolutionary adaptation, using historical data and by watching evolution happen.
This project studies how stem cells become thymus cells and whether cells from older adults can support T cell development in aged mice.
This project adds laser spectroscopy to liquid chromatography so the parts of biopharmaceutical products can be measured quickly and directly.
This project tests whether long-term treatment with mirabegron improves metabolism in obese people with prediabetes and studies how it improves insulin sensitivity.
This project studies how a protein promotes fat cell formation and whether blocking a protein that suppresses it reduces fibrosis in scleroderma patients.
This project builds imaging methods to study oxygen delivery and blood flow in the retina and brain during normal ageing and Alzheimer Disease.
This project develops gene-editing treatments for four rare neurological diseases.
This project builds a decision support tool that uses patient preferences and electronic health record notes to help people with HIV keep to their treatment.
This project tests whether less frequent, higher concentration oral immunotherapy doses are safe and work for food allergy, and studies gut features of allergic people.
This project studies how senescent cells contribute to salivary gland dysfunction in Sjögren’s syndrome.
This project tests whether weak activity in one type of brain cell causes the overactive brain circuits seen in epilepsy caused by a mutated gene.
This project builds a mobile health tool that measures blood hemoglobin levels from digital photos of the eyelid to help detect anemia in pregnancy.
This project develops imaging methods to find early on why cancer patients do not respond to immunotherapy.
This project develops an imaging and tissue test to predict which breast cancer patients will respond to a certain type of drug therapy.
This project studies whether microRNAs carried by extracellular vesicles drive atherosclerosis in people living with HIV.
This project develops a mobile microscope that detects parasitic worm eggs in wastewater, and tests it under field conditions.
